exerciseErrorRows.issue: Upward dog involves multiple joints/muscles (shoulder extension, spinal extension, hip extension) so compound is more appropriate than isolation.
Wrist extension against gravity is more of a push/extension action rather than a pull movement pattern.
Snatch is better classified as a full-body/explosive hinge-to-overhead movement; 'hinge' alone undersells the overhead punch phase, though not strictly wrong.
Compound is more appropriate given lats/biceps/traps involvement in a hang; isolation is debatable but lean minor.
Should be classified as a jump/plyometric or squat-hinge combo pattern rather than 'gait'.
Pogo hops involve ankle/knee/hip coordination and could be considered compound rather than isolation.
Leg swings are a dynamic swinging movement, not isometric; should be classified as a dynamic mobility/hip movement (e.g. 'hinge' or unclassified dynamic, not isometric).
Warrior I is a multi-joint standing pose involving hips, knees, and shoulders; better classified as compound rather than isolation.

Decline cable press setup and high pulley description is inconsistent; decline pressing typically uses low pulleys pressing upward/forward, not high pulleys pressing down, which contradicts standard decline press mechanics.
Quads listed as primary but Sots press is primarily a shoulder press with minimal quad involvement while seated in the bottom squat position; quads are more stabilizer/secondary.
Quads are heavily involved only in the initial dip/drive, not a primary target muscle for a press; better as secondary.
Tire flip is a combination hinge-to-squat/press movement, better classified as 'squat' or a compound full-body pattern, not purely 'hinge'.
Skin the cat is a dynamic rotational/pulling movement through a range, not truly isometric.
Vertical hop is better classified as a jump/plyometric pattern rather than 'gait', which implies locomotion.
Hurdle hopping involves forward locomotion so 'gait' is defensible, but could also be classified as plyometric jump; minor classification concern.
Scissor kicks involve continuous dynamic leg movement, not an isometric hold; should be classified differently (e.g., core/dynamic).
Wall sit is often classified as compound (multi-joint hip/knee) despite isometric nature; isolation is debatable but somewhat off.
Pectorals are not primary movers in cobra pose; spinal extensors (lower-back) are primary, chest is more of a stretch target.
Tuck planche is a compound, multi-joint movement (shoulders, elbows, core), not isolation.
Hip thrust is generally considered a compound movement (hip and knee involvement), not isolation.
Atlas stone lift is more of a squat/deadlift-hybrid pattern; labeling purely as hinge is debatable but not clearly wrong; flagged as minor.
Calf raise is better classified as isolation push/plantarflexion movement rather than isometric, since it involves dynamic ROM.
Power snatch is typically classified under 'olympic' or 'explosive' pattern rather than plain hinge, though hinge is part of it.
Battle rope circles involve more of a rotational/isometric shoulder pattern than a true push pattern.
Ab wheel rollout is a dynamic anti-extension core movement, better classified as isometric-anti-extension or its own category, not strictly isometric.
Hand-to-hand swing alternates but overall movement is often classified bilateral like standard swing; debatable but arguably fine as unilateral per-arm phase.
